summary: The checkout pods are repeatedly restarting with OOMKilled status because a recent deployment configuration set the container memory limit to 32Mi, while the application's startup script attempts to allocate ~38.1 MB of memory.
root_cause: The checkout deployment container has a memory limit of 32Mi, but its startup command allocates 40,000,000 bytes (~38.1 MB) into memory, exceeding the limit and causing container termination with OOMKilled (Exit Code 137).

evidence.why_it_matters: Shows that the checkout pod is failing due to OOMKilled.

evidence.excerpt:
{"name":"app","init":false,"image":"busybox:1.36","ready":false,"restart_count":1,"state":{"state":"terminated","reason":"OOMKilled","exit_code":137,...},"resources":{"requests":{"cpu":"10m","memory":"16Mi"},"limits":{"memory":"32Mi"}},"command":["sh","-c","echo "loading product catalog into memory"
catalog=$(head -c 40000000 /dev/zero | tr '\0' 'x')
echo "catalog loaded (${#catalog} bytes); serving"
sleep 3600
"]}
evidence.why_it_matters: Proves the container memory limit is 32Mi while the startup command allocates 40,000,000 bytes (~38.1 MB), directly causing OOMKilled (Exit Code 137).

proposed_fix.rationale: Increase the memory limit from 32Mi to 128Mi so that the container can successfully allocate ~38.1 MB for the product catalog without triggering an OOM kill.
proposed_fix.risk: Low. Increasing the memory limit allows the container to run successfully without OOMKilled restarts.

alternative_hypotheses: Rollout undo to the previous revision (checkout-c87575bc5) which had a higher memory limit (128Mi)
